records.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
records.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count FROM orders

records.question: How many unique customers have placed an order?
records.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

records.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo (SP)?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) AS seller_count FROM sellers WHERE seller_state = 'SP'

records.question: What is the average review score?
records.sql: SELECT AVG(review_score) AS avg_review_score FROM order_reviews

records.question: How many orders were canceled?
records.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT order_id) AS canceled_orders FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled'

records.question: How many payments were made with each payment type?
records.sql: SELECT payment_type, count(*) AS payment_count FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY payment_count DESC

records.question: What is the most common number of instalments for credit card payments?
records.sql: SELECT payment_installments, count(*) AS payment_count FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY payment_installments ORDER BY payment_count DESC LIMIT 1

records.question: How many orders were placed in 2017?
records.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_placed_2017 FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'

records.question: How many reviews were given at each review score?
records.sql: SELECT review_score, count(*) AS review_count FROM order_reviews GROUP BY review_score ORDER BY review_score

records.question: What is the total payment value for each payment type?
records.sql: SELECT payment_type, SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY total_payment_value DESC

records.question: What are the top 5 product categories by revenue? Use English category names.
records.sql: SELECT coalesce(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category, sum(oi.price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Which 5 customer states placed the most orders?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, count(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Which 5 customer states have the longest average delivery time in days?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, AVG(date_diff('second', o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date) / 86400.0) AS avg_delivery_days FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY avg_delivery_days DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Who are the top 10 sellers by revenue?
records.sql: SELECT s.seller_id, s.seller_city, s.seller_state, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_city, s.seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10

records.question: Which 5 customer states have the highest average order value?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, SUM(oi.price) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS aov FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY aov DESC LIMIT 5;

records.question: For each review score, what is the average delivery time in days?
records.sql: SELECT r.review_score, AVG(date_diff('second', o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date) / 86400.0) AS avg_delivery_days, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM orders o JOIN order_reviews r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.review_score ORDER BY r.review_score

records.question: Which 5 product categories have the highest average freight value per item? Use English names.
records.sql: SELECT coalesce(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category, avg(oi.freight_value) AS avg_freight_per_item FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name WHERE p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg_freight_per_item DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Which 5 seller states sold the most items?
records.sql: SELECT s.seller_state, count(*) AS items_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY s.seller_state ORDER BY items_sold DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: On average, how many items does an order contain?
records.sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS avg_items_per_order FROM order_items

records.question: How many orders were placed in each month from January to August 2018?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', orders.order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_month, count(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS orders_placed FROM orders WHERE orders.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND orders.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: How have sales trended month by month?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_month, sum(oi.price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: What percentage of customers are repeat customers?
records.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, count(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id) SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE n_orders >= 2) / count(*), 2) AS repeat_customer_pct FROM order_counts

records.question: What share of delivered orders arrived later than the estimated delivery date, by month in 2018?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_month, count(*) AS delivered_orders, sum(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders, round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / count(*), 2) AS late_share_pct FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: What was the month-over-month revenue growth rate in 2018, from February to August?
records.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_month, sum(oi.price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01' GROUP BY 1), with_growth AS (SELECT order_month, revenue, lag(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month) AS prev_revenue FROM monthly) SELECT order_month, revenue, prev_revenue, (revenue - prev_revenue) / prev_revenue AS mom_growth_rate FROM with_growth WHERE order_month >= '2018-02-01' AND order_month < '2018-09-01' ORDER BY order_month

records.question: Do late deliveries get worse reviews? Compare the average review score of late and on-time delivered orders.
records.sql: WITH rev AS (SELECT order_id, avg(review_score) AS score FROM order_reviews GROUP BY order_id), d AS (SELECT o.order_id, CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS delivery_status FROM orders o WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL) SELECT d.delivery_status, count(*) AS orders_with_review, avg(rev.score) AS avg_review_score FROM d JOIN rev ON rev.order_id = d.order_id GROUP BY d.delivery_status ORDER BY d.delivery_status

records.question: Among product categories with at least 1,000 reviewed orders, which 5 have the lowest average review score? Use English names.
records.sql: WITH cat_orders AS (SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, coalesce(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name WHERE p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL), reviewed AS (SELECT co.category, co.order_id, r.review_score FROM cat_orders co JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = co.order_id WHERE co.category IS NOT NULL) SELECT category, count(DISTINCT order_id) AS reviewed_orders, avg(review_score) AS avg_review_score FROM reviewed GROUP BY category HAVING count(DISTINCT order_id) >= 1000 ORDER BY avg_review_score ASC LIMIT 5

records.question: Among customer states with at least 1,000 delivered orders, which has the highest late delivery rate?
records.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT c.customer_state AS state, o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date AS is_late FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL) SELECT state, count(*) AS delivered_orders, sum(CASE WHEN is_late THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders, sum(CASE WHEN is_late THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / count(*) AS late_rate FROM d GROUP BY state HAVING count(*) >= 1000 ORDER BY late_rate DESC LIMIT 1

records.question: What share of total revenue comes from the top 10% of sellers?
records.sql: WITH seller_rev AS (SELECT oi.seller_id, SUM(oi.price) AS rev FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') GROUP BY oi.seller_id), ranked AS (SELECT seller_id, rev, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM seller_rev) SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN rn <= CEIL(0.1 * n) THEN rev ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / CAST(SUM(rev) AS DOUBLE) AS top10_pct_seller_revenue_share FROM ranked

records.question: For customers who ordered more than once, what is the average number of days between their first and second order?
records.sql: WITH o AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp AS ts, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_id) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) SELECT avg(date_diff('second', f.ts, s.ts) / 86400.0) AS avg_days_between_first_and_second_order FROM o f JOIN o s ON f.customer_unique_id = s.customer_unique_id AND f.rn = 1 AND s.rn = 2

records.question: Which 5 product categories grew revenue the most from 2017 to 2018? Compare January to August of each year, in absolute terms, using English names.
records.sql: WITH items AS (SELECT COALESCE(ct.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category, oi.price, o.order_purchase_timestamp FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation ct ON ct.product_category_name = p.product_category_name WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') AND YEAR(o.order_purchase_timestamp) IN (2017, 2018) AND MONTH(o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN 1 AND 8), by_cat AS (SELECT category, SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(order_purchase_timestamp) = 2017 THEN price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2017_jan_aug, SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(order_purchase_timestamp) = 2018 THEN price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2018_jan_aug FROM items GROUP BY category) SELECT category, revenue_2017_jan_aug, revenue_2018_jan_aug, revenue_2018_jan_aug - revenue_2017_jan_aug AS revenue_growth_abs FROM by_cat ORDER BY revenue_2018_jan_aug - revenue_2017_jan_aug DESC LIMIT 5
